title: Mixtape and Recipe
premise: Odile Eriksen, seventeen, has been holding her family together since her father left — cooking, budgeting, and raising her younger siblings while her mother works hospital night shifts. When her civics teacher pairs her with Priya Chandrasekaran, her longtime rival and the seemingly perfect daughter of a wealthy local family, for a semester project documenting 'an inheritance that shaped this town,' Odile expects misery. Instead they uncover that both their families are entangled in a decades-old land deal that enriched Priya's family by quietly displacing Odile's neighborhood — and that Priya's grandmother left behind letters confessing it. As the deadline looms and Priya's parents pressure her to bury the evidence, Odile must choose between protecting her family's fragile stability and exposing a truth that could cost them everything; in the end, the girls publish the project anyway, forcing public reckoning, and Odile learns that inheritance isn't only what's taken from you but what you choose to build.
about_author: Mirabel Iversen is a former community-college writing tutor who grew up in a rust-belt town much like the one in her debut. She writes stories about kids who are older than they should have to be, and she still makes her grandmother's soup recipe every Sunday.

chapters.title: Everything Is Fine
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. A chaotic morning: burnt toast, little brother Milo's lost permission slip, sister Bea's silent fury, mom home from nights. Odile runs the household like a drill sergeant and insists to everyone — including herself — that she doesn't need help. Emotional beat: loving exhaustion disguised as competence.

chapters.title: The Pairing Nobody Asked For
chapters.summary: In civics class, Ms. Okafor announces semester projects and reads names aloud: Eriksen and Chandrasekaran. Odile and Priya exchange venom across the room, history stretching back to middle school. Odile calculates how to survive this without letting anyone see her life is held together with tape. Beat: dread sharpened into defiance.

chapters.title: Terms of Engagement
chapters.summary: First library meeting. They negotiate like hostile nations: split the work, no personal questions. Priya suggests researching the old Harrow Street mill district — Odile stiffens; that's her neighborhood. She agrees anyway because the topic earns top marks. Beat: wary truce with an undercurrent of something unspoken.

chapters.title: Recipe Card, Coffee Ring
chapters.summary: At home, Odile cooks from her late grandmother's recipe box while helping Milo with homework. A flashback shows Grandma Eriksen telling stories about Harrow Street before 'the change.' Odile realizes the mill district assignment might be closer to home than she admitted. Beat: tenderness and the first crack in her armor.

chapters.title: The House on Alder Lane
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya's immaculate house, distant parents, and a locked study where her grandmother Nani's belongings sit boxed after her death. Priya finds a bundle of unsent letters mentioning Harrow Street and a name: Eriksen. She hides them. Beat: loneliness inside privilege.

chapters.title: Archive Dust
chapters.summary: Joint POV alternating at the county archive. Old deeds show Priya's grandfather bought whole blocks of Harrow Street in 1994 for pennies through a shell company, right before rezoning. Odile recognizes her own street. They argue about what it means; neither says the obvious. Beat: discovery as slow-burning alarm.

chapters.title: Labels
chapters.summary: School scenes: classmates assume rich girl carries poor girl. Odile snaps at Priya publicly; Priya, stung, goes cold. Odile's mom picks up extra shifts; Odile cancels a meeting to cover childcare and lies about why. Beat: the old labels reasserting themselves just as they started to loosen.

chapters.title: Letters Unsent
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. She reads more of Nani's letters: her grandmother knew about the displacement, protested within the family, was silenced, and kept paying anonymous rent support to one displaced family — the Eriksens. Priya is shaken and, for the first time, angry at her own name. Beat: inherited guilt igniting.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Copy Machine
chapters.summary: Priya confronts Odile: did your family know? Odile bristles at being a charity case, then learns Grandma Eriksen's mysterious 'church fund' was Nani all along. The girls' fight cracks open into raw honesty about their families. Beat: enemies becoming witnesses to each other.

chapters.title: Midterm Check-In
chapters.summary: Ms. Okafor praises their preliminary work and warns against 'safe conclusions.' Meanwhile Priya's father, Vikram, asks pointed questions about the project topic and tells her some history is better left descriptive, not accusatory. Beat: pressure mounting from above and within.

chapters.title: Bea Runs
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Bea skips school; Odile finds her at the demolished mill site. Bea explodes: she's tired of Odile playing parent, tired of being managed. Odile realizes her control is its own kind of power — and its own kind of corruption. Beat: found-family theme turned inward on blood family.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Vikram Chandrasekaran offers Odile's mother a well-paid job managing his new development — contingent, subtly, on the project staying 'balanced.' Mom, exhausted, wants to take it. Odile sees the trap clearly and can't say so without sounding ungrateful. Beat: corruption arriving politely, with paperwork.

chapters.title: Study Session, Actual Studying
chapters.summary: A quiet chapter: the girls work at Odile's kitchen table, Milo quizzing them on flashcards, Priya learning the choreography of the Eriksen household. Priya admits she envies the noise and love. Odile admits she envies the silence and safety. Beat: friendship solidifying over shared hunger.

chapters.title: The Missing Box
chapters.summary: The letters disappear from Priya's room; her father admits he 'archived' them. Priya realizes she's been backed into the same corner Nani was. She secretly photographed everything weeks ago — a habit learned from watching her parents. Beat: the heir choosing which inheritance to keep.

chapters.title: Deadline Pressure
chapters.summary: Two weeks to presentation. Odile wavers: publishing the truth could tank the job offer and expose her family's finances to scrutiny. Priya pushes; Odile accuses her of spending someone else's stability. Their worst fight yet. Beat: the cost of truth made concrete.

chapters.title: What Grandma Kept
chapters.summary: Odile opens Grandma Eriksen's recipe box fully and finds clippings, a deed stub, and a note: 'Tell it straight, Dilly, even when it costs.' She understands her grandmother never wanted quiet compensation — she wanted witness. Beat: inheritance reframed as obligation to truth.

chapters.title: The Night Before
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Priya drafts a statement disowning her family's version of events; Odile preps the presentation while mom hesitates over the job contract, unsigned. Milo asks why Odile looks scared, and she finally answers honestly: 'Because I don't know who I'll be tomorrow.' Beat: hush before the storm.

chapters.title: Presentation Day
chapters.summary: Climax. In front of class, invited parents, and Ms. Okafor, the girls present 'Mixtape and Recipe': oral histories, the 1994 deeds, Nani's letters. Vikram walks out; Priya keeps speaking. Odile names her own street and her grandmother's name aloud. Beat: courage as public, irreversible act.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Fallout: local paper picks it up, the job offer evaporates, school buzzes, Bea grudgingly admits Odile fought for something real. Mom, furious then thoughtful, signs onto a tenants' coalition instead. Beat: consequences landing, identity holding.

chapters.title: Hearing
chapters.summary: A city hearing on reopening the old land titles. Odile testifies, voice shaking; Priya testifies against her own family's interest. Vikram, cornered, offers a settlement including restitution — proof that exposure, not politeness, moved him. Beat: power answering to accountability.

chapters.title: Sunday Soup
chapters.summary: Resolution. Weeks later: the Eriksen kitchen, Priya chopping vegetables like she belongs there, Bea laughing, mom home on a Sunday for once. Odile adds a new card to the recipe box — in her own handwriting. Beat: found family braided into blood family.

chapters.title: Mixtape and Recipe
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Odile's POV. Graduation approaches; Ms. Okafor returns their graded project with a single line: 'This is who you are when the labels come off.' Odile mails a copy of the project to the county archive, filed under Harrow Street. Beat: inheritance claimed, future authored.
